name: Trinidad and the Valley de los Ingenios
description: Trinidad is a colonial town on Cuba's south-central coast, founded in the early 1500s and once a launching point for Spanish expeditions to the mainland. Sugar wealth paid for its pastel mansions, such as the Palacio Brunet and Palacio Cantero, which line its cobbled streets. Nearby, the Valle de los Ingenios holds the ruins of more than 70 sugar mills, worked by some 30,000 enslaved people at the industry's peak.
